meta.test_method: Claude in Chrome — live browser interaction
meta.shayla_one_liner: It's got potential but right now it feels like a developer's side project, not a product I'd recommend to my team.

scenarios.name: First Impression & Signup
findings: POSITIVE: Landing URL redirects straight to /chat — no friction, no marketing page gatekeeping. Shayla is in the product immediately.
POSITIVE: UI is localized in Mongolian. Navigation labels (Чат, Төслүүд, Insights, Төлбөр, Үнэ) all render correctly in Cyrillic.
POSITIVE: Brand name 'MultiModel' is visible in the top-left. Clean, warm color palette (teal + cream). Looks professional, not generic.
POSITIVE: Free plan badge and credit balance (1.00 USD) are visible in the sidebar — Shayla knows her limits immediately.
NEGATIVE: Could not test signup/login flow because the session was already authenticated. The login page experience remains untested.
NEGATIVE: No onboarding tour or first-use guidance. Shayla is dropped into a chat with a previous conversation visible — no 'Welcome, here's how to get started' moment.
scenarios.shayla_reaction: OK, it loaded fast and it's in Mongolian — that's already better than most AI tools. But what am I supposed to do first? There's no guidance.

scenarios.name: First Chat — Can She Get Value in 2 Minutes?
findings: POSITIVE: 'Шинэ чат' (New Chat) button is prominent and easy to find.

POSITIVE: Quick action chips are localized and marketing-relevant: 'Лэндинг хуудасны текст' (Landing page text), 'Кампанит ажлын товч' (Campaign brief), 'A/B test санаа' (A/B test ideas). These are exactly what Shayla needs.
POSITIVE: Cost estimate shown BEFORE sending: 'Тооцоолсон үнэ: 0.04 USD (4 загвар)'. Excellent transparency.
POSITIVE: The unified response ('Нэгдсэн хариу') produced 3 Mongolian ad headlines in 3.7 seconds. The output quality was actually good and work-relevant.
POSITIVE: Flow diagram showing prompt → models → unified response is visually clear and helps explain the multi-model concept.
CRITICAL: Claude Sonnet 4 card shows raw error: 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not configured'. Gemini 2.5 Flash shows: 'GOOGLE_API_KEY is not configured'. Both have red/pink error borders.
CRITICAL: These are developer-facing error messages exposed directly to an end user. Shayla has no idea what an API key is. She sees 2 out of 3 models 'broken' with technical jargon.
NEGATIVE: The product claims '4 загвар' (4 models) but only GPT-4.1 actually responded. Where is the 4th model? The math doesn't add up.
scenarios.shayla_reaction: Wait — it says 4 models but only one actually worked? And what is 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not configured'? Is this thing broken? I thought the whole point was multiple AI models.
scenarios.recommendation: URGENT: Never show raw API key errors to users. Replace with: 'Энэ загвар одоогоор боломжгүй байна' (This model is currently unavailable). Better yet, don't show unavailable models in the response flow at all — only show models that successfully responded.

scenarios.name: Collaboration Modes Discovery
findings: POSITIVE: 'Нэгдсэн хариу' (Unified response) mode is the default and works correctly as a concept — prompt fans out to multiple models, responses are unified.
POSITIVE: Settings gear icon (⚙️) is visible next to the mode banner for configuration.
POSITIVE: The mode banner explains itself: '4 загвар · Загвар тус бүрийн нооргоор болон нэгтгэсэн эцсийн хариу' (4 models · Draft from each model and a unified final response). This is clear.
NEGATIVE: Only 'Ерөнхий' (General) mode was visible in the top bar. The other modes (Debate, Expert, Simulation, etc.) were not immediately discoverable without clicking the gear icon.
NEGATIVE: The mode names 'Ensemble', 'Debate', 'Expert' are likely English-only terms. Shayla might not understand them without Mongolian translations.
scenarios.shayla_reaction: I see it says 'Unified response' and there's a settings icon. I guess I can change modes? But I don't know what my options are without clicking around.

scenarios.name: Mobile Responsiveness
findings: CRITICAL: At 375px viewport width, the sidebar (~290px fixed width) does not collapse or hide. It consumes approximately 77% of the screen width, leaving only ~85px for the chat content area.
CRITICAL: No hamburger menu, no collapsible sidebar, no responsive breakpoint detected. The layout is a fixed desktop layout that does not adapt to mobile screens.
NEGATIVE: Quick action chips in the chat input area would overflow horizontally on mobile with no visible scroll indicator.
NEGATIVE: The model selector dropdown at ~300px width would be unusable on a 375px screen.
scenarios.shayla_reaction: I can't show this to my boss on my phone. It's desktop-only. In 2026, that's not acceptable.
scenarios.recommendation: Implement responsive breakpoints: sidebar should collapse to a hamburger menu at < 768px. Chat input should stack vertically. Model selector needs a mobile-friendly sheet/modal.

scenarios.name: Pricing & Billing Clarity
findings: POSITIVE: Pricing page is accessible from sidebar via 'Үнэ' (Price) button. Navigation is intuitive.
POSITIVE: 4 clear tiers: Free, Plus ($19), Pro ($49, marked 'Хамгийн түгээмэл' — Most popular), Team ($129).
POSITIVE: USD/MNT currency toggle — Shayla can see prices in Mongolian Tugrik (67,802 MNT for Plus, 174,859 MNT for Pro). This is a killer feature for local market adoption.
POSITIVE: Monthly/Yearly toggle present.
POSITIVE: Each tier clearly shows: monthly credit allowance, number of active models, feature checklist with green checkmarks vs. dashes.
POSITIVE: Dashboard has dedicated Usage, Billing, and Plans sub-sections — well-organized.
MINOR: '/cap' label after prices is ambiguous — does it mean per capita? per month? Shayla might not know.
scenarios.shayla_reaction: Finally, a pricing page I can screenshot and send to my team lead. The MNT conversion is actually impressive — most AI tools don't even know Mongolia exists.

scenarios.name: Template Discovery
findings: CRITICAL: Template Library page is completely empty. 'No templates yet. Create one or seed system templates to get started.'

CRITICAL: Clicking 'Seed System Templates' triggers a raw PostgreSQL error: 'there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification'. This is a database error exposed directly to the end user.
NEGATIVE: Template Library header, search bar, and empty state text are all in English — breaking the Mongolian localization pattern established elsewhere in the app.
NEGATIVE: 'Seed System Templates' is developer jargon. Shayla would never know what 'seed' means in this context.
NEGATIVE: No pre-built marketing templates exist. For a user whose workflow is 'create campaign briefs and A/B test ideas', this is a missed opportunity.
scenarios.shayla_reaction: There's an error when I click the button and there are no templates at all? This page is broken. And why is it suddenly in English?
scenarios.recommendation: 1. Fix the ON CONFLICT database migration immediately. 2. Pre-populate with 10-15 templates across categories (Marketing, Development, Writing, Analysis). 3. Localize the entire Template Library page to Mongolian. 4. Rename 'Seed System Templates' to 'Загвар нэмэх' (Add templates) or similar.

scenarios.name: Error Handling & Edge Cases
findings: POSITIVE: 404 page is clean and user-friendly: icon, '404 Page not found', 'The page you're looking for doesn't exist or has been moved.', 'Go home' button. Clear recovery path.
NEGATIVE: 404 page is entirely in English — no Mongolian localization.
NEGATIVE: 404 page has no MultiModel branding (no logo, no brand colors). Shayla might think she navigated away from the product entirely.
CRITICAL: API key errors (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY) are shown raw in the chat flow diagram. No user-friendly error handling.
CRITICAL: PostgreSQL error on Template seeding is shown raw. No error boundary or graceful fallback.
SUMMARY: The app handles routing errors (404) gracefully but fails completely on API/database errors — the exact errors a user is most likely to encounter during actual usage.
scenarios.shayla_reaction: The 404 page is fine but the real errors — the ones I actually hit while using the product — are raw technical garbage. That's backwards.

option_b_value_proposition_verdict.core_question: Even if every bug were fixed tomorrow, does Shayla NEED Multi-Model AI?
option_b_value_proposition_verdict.verdict: CONDITIONAL YES — but only if multi-model comparison actually works

what_shayla_has_today.chatgpt: Free, reliable, good for daily questions and text generation. She knows it well.
what_shayla_has_today.gemini: Free, good for image generation. Her go-to for visual marketing assets.
what_shayla_has_today.pain_point: Switching between tabs, copy-pasting the same prompt into both, no side-by-side comparison

what_multimodel_promises.value_proposition: Query multiple AI models with one prompt, get a unified best-of response
what_multimodel_promises.pricing_for_shayla: Free tier: 1.00 USD credit, 1 active model. Plus tier: $19/month for 2 active models.
what_multimodel_promises.key_insight: The FREE tier only gives her 1 active model — which means she gets LESS than what she has today (ChatGPT + Gemini for free). She'd need to pay $19/month just to match her current 2-tool setup.

the_hard_truth: Multi-Model AI's entire value proposition is 'use multiple AI models in one place'. But right now, 2 out of 3 models showed API errors. The one feature that justifies this product's existence is broken.
The free tier with 1 model is actually WORSE than Shayla's current setup (2 free tools). She has to pay to get what she already has for free.
The MNT pricing and Mongolian localization are genuine differentiators — no other AI aggregator does this. But differentiation means nothing if the core feature doesn't work.
The quick action chips (Landing page text, Campaign brief, A/B test ideas) show product-market fit awareness for marketers. But the empty template library and broken seeding undercut this.
The unified response flow diagram is genuinely innovative UX. When it works (GPT-4.1 alone), the output is good. But showing errored models in the flow diagram actively damages trust.
The cost transparency (showing estimated price before sending) is excellent and rare. This is a real selling point once the multi-model feature actually works.
shayla_would_switch_if: All 3+ models consistently respond without errors
The unified response is noticeably better than any single model alone
Templates exist for her marketing workflow
The Plus plan ($19) delivers enough credit for her weekly usage
She can show it to colleagues on mobile
shayla_would_NOT_switch_if: She has to pay $19/month for something ChatGPT + Gemini do for free
Multi-model responses keep failing with technical errors
The product feels like a developer tool, not a marketer's tool
She can't use it on her phone

option_b_value_proposition_verdict.bottom_line: You've built the right product for the right persona in the right market (Mongolian localization is a moat). But the product is shipping a promise it can't keep right now. Fix the multi-model reliability first — everything else is secondary.

priority_fix_list.issue: API key errors exposed to users (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY)
priority_fix_list.impact: Destroys the core value proposition. Users see the multi-model feature as broken.
priority_fix_list.fix: 1. Never show raw API errors. 2. Gracefully degrade: hide failed models from the flow diagram, show only successful responses. 3. If ALL models fail, show a localized error: 'Загварууд одоогоор ажиллахгүй байна. Дараа дахин оролдоно уу.'

priority_fix_list.impact: The entire Template feature is broken. Empty library + database error = dead feature.
priority_fix_list.fix: Fix the ON CONFLICT migration. Pre-populate with system templates. This should be a 1-hour database fix.

priority_fix_list.priority: P1 — Must fix before marketing push
priority_fix_list.impact: Product is unusable on phones. In Mongolia's mobile-first market, this eliminates a huge portion of potential users.
priority_fix_list.fix: Add responsive breakpoints: collapsible sidebar at < 768px, mobile-friendly model selector, stacked chat input.

priority_fix_list.priority: P1 — Must fix before marketing push
priority_fix_list.impact: Template Library, 404 page, and some model descriptions are English-only. Breaks the trust built by the Mongolian chat UI.
priority_fix_list.fix: Audit all pages for untranslated strings. Prioritize: Template Library, 404, error messages, model descriptions.

priority_fix_list.issue: No onboarding flow for first-time users
priority_fix_list.impact: Shayla gets dropped into the chat with no guidance. She has to discover features by clicking around.
priority_fix_list.fix: Add a 3-step onboarding tooltip: 1. 'Энд мессеж бичнэ' (Write a message here), 2. 'Загвар сонгох' (Select a model), 3. 'Олон загвар нэгэн зэрэг' (Multiple models at once).

priority_fix_list.impact: Minor — but Shayla might think she left the site.
priority_fix_list.fix: Add MultiModel logo and brand colors to the 404 page.

priority_fix_list.impact: Shayla might not understand it means 'per month'.
priority_fix_list.fix: Change to '/сар' (per month) in Mongolian, or '/mo' in English.

what_shayla_got_right_about_this_product: Mongolian localization is a genuine competitive moat — no other AI aggregator does this
MNT currency on the pricing page is chef's kiss for local market adoption
The quick action chips show deep understanding of marketing workflows
Cost transparency before sending is rare and valuable
The unified response flow diagram is innovative and visually clear UX
Model selection dropdown is well-organized by provider with clear labels
